lines.en: I knock on Makoto’s door and wait for her to answer. But, based on just how silent it is behind said door, it’s possible she’s not even home at all.
At the very least, Miku’s definitely not here because I don’t think she’s ever been quiet at any point in her life.
: Come in!
Well fuck me, I guess.
I turn the handle and open the door, only to be met by a wave of humid air pushing itself out of the bedroom and into my face.
But I am gifted with a wonderful sight that makes me immediately forget what I was about to complain about.
: Yo!
: Welcome to nudity.
: Am I interrupting something? I knew things were a little too quiet in here, but I didn’t think-
: Sorry to let you down, but no. You weren’t interrupting anything. Miku and I were just reading.
: You really expect me to believe that Miku knows how to read?
: Tsk, tsk, tsk. I’ll have you know I can read at a fourth grade level, Sensei. Most of the time, at least.
: Why do you look so proud of yourself?
: So...do you two always strip down to your underwear while you read? Or is this some new sort of...ritual for you?
: Since you apparently can’t tell by how disgusting it is in here, our AC unit is busted and we need to wait for it to get fixed.
: Methinks Makoto broke it herself as an excuse for fanservice. Either way, don’t matter to me! I thrive in the warmth!
: And I want to die. But I suppose that’s not really a new development and is only exacerbated by the temperature.
: I don’t mind who or what you exacerbate so long as ya do it under the blanket.
: Help me.
: Sure. Shall we resume this conversation under the blanket?
: As if I’d be able to survive under the blanket when I’m struggling to get by as-is. One more layer would surely spell my demise.
: So...it would be fine if you removed a layer?
: Again, ain’t gonna bother me! That ain’t the most flatterin’ underwear anyway, Makoto. Go ahead and take it off so you two crazy kids can exasperate all over each other.
: First, it was “exacerbate.” Which you were already confusing with “masturbate.” But, more importantly than that, how are you going to talk down on my underwear when you’re wearing that?
: Tsk, tsk, tsk. Ya seem to be missin’ the whole point of this get-up, Makoto.
: What is it with you and these “tsk tsk tsks” today? And yes, I am likely missing the point. Unless the point is that normal bras just don’t fit you yet.
: That...is partially true! But the truer thingy I was gettin’ at is that sports bras and lil’ tanktop thingies fit gals with this body type better than anythin’! Ain’t that right, Sensei?
: The only way I can know for sure is by physically examining you.
: As you please.
: I’m not allowed, am I?
: Correct. You are not allowed.
: Sorry, Miku. Maybe next time.
: Fine by me. I was about to leave you two alone anyway. Lots more studyin’ to catch up on since Makoto’s been crackin’ down on me lately.
: But hey, maybe I’ll make it up to fifth grade level by the end of the year! That’d be neat!
: Works for me. Maybe I could even whisk Makoto away or something since she’s apparently dying in here?
: Whisk me away to where? The underwear store? You know, since you and Miku apparently hate my bra.
: Don’t lump me in with her. I think your bra is entirely...adequate.
: Wow, how flattering.
Makoto and Miku head back to their beds and I follow the “vibe” of the room by making my way over to Makoto’s as well.
Now, I know you’re probably wondering what a “vibe” is. And to that, I say...
Same.
But I’m pretty sure it means a “feeling” and I’m pretty sure the feeling in here is that I’m supposed to be hanging out with Makoto, so yeah.
: Upon closer inspection, I kind of like your underwear.
: I’m pretty sure you just kind of like my ass.
: It’s a good ass.
: What do you want, Sensei?
: I want to hang out with my new best friend, Makoto Miyamura. Who is also known as “The girl I’m going to be worryingly nice to from now on.”
: Any amount of niceties from you is worrying. Which is why I asked you what you want. But if you’re just here to spend time with me and stare at my butt, I guess that’s fine too.
: Do you not want to leave? I was ready to head out for an exciting night on the town with you.
: To be honest, I kind of want to read my book. Which isn’t me directly saying I want you to leave, but...
: If you just so happened to leave right now, I wouldn’t be all that torn up inside.
: What happened to the Makoto who used to cling to me like Velcro?
: A lot. Where have you been the last few months?
: Not spending enough time with you apparently. Which is precisely why I will refuse to leave right now so we can make up for lost time. Your book can wait.
: Fine. But only because you’re very rarely this pushy when it comes to me and I think it’s kind of cute to have you doing that instead of pushing back for once.
: I can assure you it’s all part of my master plan to shape you into the perfect bride.
: Don’t tempt me with a good time, Sensei. Jokes like that don’t always stay jokes forever, you know. You could be unintentionally foreshadowing something right now.
: At the same time, not all dialogue has to be foreshadowing- but I suppose we can leave that at that for now.
: What would you like to discuss instead? I think I’m all drama’ed out for the time being. Plus, Miku is right across the room, so we can’t exactly talk about her again.
: Huh? You two were talkin’ about me? When?
: Whenever the last time you lied to me was.
: I ain’t got any idea what yer talkin’ about, so...I’m just gonna keep on reading.
: Subtle.
: For now. I’m keeping an eye out.
: Well, since you’re all drama’ed out and Miku is out of the discussion, I guess...you can tell me about your day?
: Ew. Can you start a little slower if you’re going to be nice from now on? Acting so uncharacteristic right off the bat is throwing me off.
: I’m bad at being casual and friendly and all of my regular conversation topics are either all about me or just way too sexual to maintain without throwing myself on top of you.
: Under the blanket’s okay! Just wanna remind ya!
: Thanks, Miku. Appreciated.
: Standard small talk it is then, but...how even was my day?
: It feels like it kind of ended without anything interesting happening.
: The day itself was fine...I helped Miss Imai reorganize all of the desks after class...Then I helped her clean the locker room....Then I helped her mop the pool room...And I think that was it.
: Well here’s hoping you don’t fall for her next, I guess. Having someone else steal away my one and only teacher’s pet sounds like something I don’t want to deal with.
: You’re only saying that because I do all of your work for you.
: There are other benefits as well. I just can’t talk about them until we’re underneath the blanket.
: Oh, and there was something with Yumi as well. I completely forgot, but she actually asked me for help with something earlier. Math, I think.
: Hey, there’s a conversation topic. What’s going on with you and Yumi?
: Uhh...nothing? I just helped her with some equation. It’s not like we’re going to the Spring Fling together. Especially on account of spring literally not existing here.
: I’m talking more about how you helped get her suspension revoked. Why?
: What do you mean why? What kind of future-teacher would I be if I just let someone who needs help get kicked out of school? That goes against everything I stand for.
: So...it wasn’t just because you wanted to get revenge on Nodoka for-
: Please do not bring up my embarrassing defeat in the first Dorm Wars. Especially in a way that makes it sound like I would wish bodily harm upon her for just outsmarting me.
: Though, it would be nice if she’d leave me alone in the shower...
: I really wish you guys would invite me in there one day. It’s one of the only places I haven’t gone yet.
: Here’s hoping it remains that way. But anyway, the point is that I just didn’t think it was fair to indefinitely suspend her.
: I think that if a student wants to learn, she or he should be given the tools to do so. And Yumi wouldn’t have come back if she didn’t want to. I just made it a little easier for her to do that.
: Well, thank you for once again going out of your way to help someone who is both resistant to help and doesn’t deserve it.
: What can I say? That sort of thing is becoming a bit of a specialty to me.
: Why are you taking so much interest in this, though? You seemed pretty indifferent around the time I brought it up.
: Yeah, but that’s probably because I was in the middle of trying to reset the world and that it wasn’t something I was entirely conscious for.
: If you’re quoting something right now, I don’t get the reference. I don’t really watch TV.
: Don’t mind me. Just talking about how the world is part of a never-ending cycle and that we’re doomed to relive this school year over and over and over again for the rest of our lives.
: Again, not getting the reference. But I don’t think I’d mind having you as my teacher for the rest of eternity.
: And I’m not just saying that because you singlehandedly prevent me from ever having to exacerbate.
: Well, I’m glad this relationship is mutually beneficial for the both of us. It’s just one more thing for me to look forward to as my apocalypse counter begins to tick upward.
: I didn’t realize you believed in that sort of thing, Sensei. Though, just to clarify, you are talking about the apocalypse in a more biblical sense, correct? Not a natural one?
: Correct. There’s no way a natural phenomenon could possibly explain how-
: Wait...why aren’t you changing the subject?
: Because...I’m polite? And actually capable of carrying on a normal conversation when the person I’m talking to isn’t busy shoving his hands down my pants?
: No, I just mean that...uhh...extenuating circumstances prevent anyone else from ever being able to talk about this without immediately changing the topic.
: Sensei, I’m only saying this because I’m allowed to be mean to you now...but what the fuck are you talking about?
: I’m talking about how this shouldn’t be possible with anyone other than Maya and Ayane...and yet here you are, perfectly navigating the talk as if it’s something you’ve known all along.
: Known what? Why are you being so weird?
: Because this is what happens anytime I talk about this with anyone else. Watch.
: Miku.
: Hm? Yeah?
: Every few months, the world starts over and everyone-
: Oh! Sensei! I forgot to tell ya about this crazy thing that happened at swim practice the other day! Ya have a sec? Or are you still too busy kickin’ it with my best friendo?
: See? She immediately changed the topic.
: This is Miku we’re talking about. She can’t stay focused on anything.
: You try then. See what happens.
: Miku, what-
: Oh! You and me should go bra shoppin’ soon, Makoto! We can get ya somethin’ that looks like it hasn’t been through the wash eight thousand times.
: Shut up and listen to me for a second, okay?
: Okay! Sure!
: Sensei thinks that the world is-
: Oh! You and me should go bra shoppin’ soon, Makoto! We can get ya somethin’ that looks like it hasn’t been through the wash eight thousand times.
: ...what?
: See what I mean?
: You two are...playing some weird kind of prank on me, right?
: Miku-
: Oh! Sensei! I forgot to tell ya about this crazy thing that happened at swim practice the other day! Ya have a sec? Or are you still too busy kickin’ it with my best friendo?
: Oh! You and me should go bra shoppin’ soon, Makoto! We can get ya somethin’ that looks like it hasn’t been through the wash eight thousand times.
: I don’t get it...why won’t she let us get our thoughts out?
: I don’t get it either. But it’s not just her. It’s everyone except you and the two girls I mentioned earlier.
: And, for a brief moment in time, Yumi and Tsuneyo as well.
: The reason I don’t remember you bringing up whatever it was you did to get Yumi back into school is because I was never there for it.
: You were, though. I saw you. We...We talked and everything.
: Then why don’t I remember any of it?
: Because...your memories are bad. They’ve been bad every single year since we’ve started-
: But...wait...I’m a freshman...how have we...
: Am I just...
: What?
: I have to make a phone call.
: You might want to get dressed.
